text.label: Text: Who It Is For
text.value: Who It Is For

text.label: Heading: This book was written for two people. You are probably one o
text.value: This book was written for two people. You are probably one of them.

text.label: Text: The spot you are in.
text.value: The spot you are in.

text.label: Text: You are a coach, an author, a speaker or an influencer. You
text.value: You are a coach, an author, a speaker or an influencer. You know something other people want to learn, and you have spent years getting good at it. People watch you. Some of them quote you back to yourself. And when you look at your bank account, it does not look like your follower count. If that is you, nothing is wrong with you and nothing is wrong with what you teach. You are standing in a spot a lot of talented people are standing in, and nobody ever showed you the way out of it.

text.label: Text: An audience, nothing to sell.
text.value: An audience, nothing to sell.

text.label: Text: The first version of that spot is a crowd with nothing to bu
text.value: The first version of that spot is a crowd with nothing to buy. You have 5,000, 10,000, maybe 50,000 followers. They like what you say. They would pay you for more of it if there were something to pay for. There is not. No program, no course, no book with your name on the cover. So the attention arrives every day and leaves every day, and all you have to show for it is a number on a screen that belongs to somebody else.

text.label: Text: Something to sell, no hours.
text.value: Something to sell, no hours.

text.label: Text: The second version is harder to see, because money is coming
text.value: The second version is harder to see, because money is coming in. You have a program or a course, and it sells. But it only sells when you answer every message yourself. A person asks what it costs on a Saturday night, and you see it three days later. You make sales when you launch something, and it goes quiet in between. You could not hand me ten names and phone numbers of the people watching you. The business works exactly as hard as you do, and it stops when you stop.

text.label: Text: The two readers.
text.value: The two readers.

text.label: Text: Chapter one talks to two readers in turn. One has built an a
text.value: Chapter one talks to two readers in turn. One has built an audience and is missing everything that goes behind it. The other has no audience yet. I tell that second reader something they do not expect: you are not behind. You get to build the system first and open the doors after, the way a franchise is built. The first stranger who ever finds you will have a place to land, a way to leave a name and something to buy. Most people with big followings cannot say that.

text.label: Text: Not a talent problem.
text.value: Not a talent problem.

text.label: Text: I want to be plain about this, because you may have been bla
text.value: I want to be plain about this, because you may have been blaming yourself. Getting attention is one skill. Turning it into income is a different skill. Being very good at the first tells you nothing about the second. The people I talk to are clearly good at what they do. What is missing is the part that goes behind the audience, and that part can be written down, in order, in plain words. That is what this book is.

text.label: Text: What A Blueprint Is
text.value: What A Blueprint Is

text.label: Heading: A blueprint is the whole plan. This one is the plan for your
text.value: A blueprint is the whole plan. This one is the plan for your entire business.

text.label: Text: The whole plan.
text.value: The whole plan.

text.label: Text: Think about what a blueprint does for a house. It shows ever
text.value: Think about what a blueprint does for a house. It shows every room, where the doors go, what holds the roof up, and the order the work gets done in. Nobody lays a floor before the foundation. A blueprint is not a tip about windows. It is the whole plan, on paper, before anybody picks up a hammer. This book does that for your business. It is the plan for how a person who knows something gets paid for it, start to finish, in the order it gets built.

text.label: Text: Not one tactic.
text.value: Not one tactic.

text.label: Text: You have probably bought tactics before. How to grow on one
text.value: You have probably bought tactics before. How to grow on one platform. How to write a caption. How to run an ad. Every one of those is a room, and some of them are good rooms. The trouble is that a room with no house around it does nothing for you. More views with nowhere to send the viewer is a good day and an empty bank account. The book never hands you a room without showing you where it sits in the house.

text.label: Text: One line.
text.value: One line.

text.label: Text: The whole model fits in one line, and it sits under the titl
text.value: The whole model fits in one line, and it sits under the title on the cover. Attention + Your Product = Dollars. Attention is the people watching and listening to you. Your product is what you know, packaged so a person can buy it. Dollars are what you get when you send the first to the second, on a website you own. Attention by itself does not pay you. A product by itself does not pay you either. A good course nobody hears about is a store on a road with no cars.

text.label: Text: Every part of it.
text.value: Every part of it.

text.label: Text: So the blueprint covers all of it. How you get the attention
text.value: So the blueprint covers all of it. How you get the attention, on platforms that send you no bill. How you take what is in your head and turn it into something with a name and a price. Where the sale happens, which is a website with your name in the address. And the six business systems behind that website that answer every person, follow up, ask for the review and ask for the sale. Connected, those six are one Revenue Engine. That is a business model, front to back.

text.label: Text: A blueprint is not a house.
text.value: A blueprint is not a house.

text.label: Text: I will say this now so nobody is surprised later. A blueprin
text.value: I will say this now so nobody is surprised later. A blueprint is the plan. It is not the house. Somebody still has to build. That can be you, on your own time. It can be a helper you pay, working from the chapters. What the blueprint gives you is the plan itself: what goes where, what comes first, and how to check that each piece works before you build the next one on top of it.

text.label: Text: Why Now
text.value: Why Now

text.label: Heading: None of this is new. What is new is that one person can affo
text.value: None of this is new. What is new is that one person can afford all of it.

text.label: Text: An old idea.
text.value: An old idea.

text.label: Text: I did not invent any of this, and the book says so in its fi
text.value: I did not invent any of this, and the book says so in its first pages. Get people's attention. Have something to sell them. Stay in front of them until they are ready. Every business I have owned ran on that. The book goes back to a hamburger stand in the 1950s, where two brothers built a way of working that anybody could be taught to run, and to the author who later gave the idea a name: the franchise prototype. The system runs the business. People run the system.

text.label: Text: What it used to take.
text.value: What it used to take.

text.label: Text: Here is why that idea was never yours to use. In 1986, the y
text.value: Here is why that idea was never yours to use. In 1986, the year I opened a restaurant, a business reached people by paying for it. A radio spot, a newspaper ad, a television spot if you could afford one. When the money stopped, the audience stopped with it. And once people did call, you needed a staff to answer them. A system like that took a building, a payroll and an advertising budget. A person whose whole business is something they know had none of the three.

text.label: Text: Free airtime.
text.value: Free airtime.

text.label: Text: Today you can go live on five different social media platfor
text.value: Today you can go live on five different social media platforms and nobody sends you a bill. That is radio and television airtime, every day, for anybody holding a phone. A podcast costs next to nothing once it is set up. You can publish your own book and sell it from your own website. The people who used to decide who got seen have lost that job. I have watched forty years of tools arrive, and never in that time has so much been available to one person at such a low price.

text.label: Text: The work gets done.
text.value: The work gets done.

text.label: Text: The second change is the bigger one. Every tool I ever put t
text.value: The second change is the bigger one. Every tool I ever put to work made a person faster. The fax did not write the letter. The website did not answer the question. A human still had to do the job, which is why growing always meant hiring. An AI employee is the first tool in forty years that does the work. It reads the message, writes back, and books a time on your calendar, at 11:40 on a Saturday night. That is what took the payroll out of the plan.

text.label: Text: So why not you.
text.value: So why not you.

text.label: Text: If you are truly an expert at what you do, there should be n
text.value: If you are truly an expert at what you do, there should be no reason you are not making money from it today. I mean that kindly. The stages cost nothing and the staff is no longer a payroll. What is left is two things. The dots have not been connected, so your attention and your product never meet. And the world has not been told. Plenty of very good people are waiting to be discovered. Nobody is coming to discover you. That job is yours now.

text.label: Text: The plain word.
text.value: The plain word.

text.label: Text: There is a plain word for telling the world, and I use it in
text.value: There is a plain word for telling the world, and I use it in the book. Self-promotion. People cannot buy from somebody they have never heard of. For most of my working life that meant buying an ad. Today it means showing up and teaching what you know, where people are already watching, with every clip pointing home to the website you own. It does not matter what you do for a living. You have to do it. The book shows you how to do it on a schedule, so it does not eat your week.

text.label: Text: The reps are yours.
text.value: The reps are yours.

text.label: Text: Here is the honest split. Getting good at what you teach too
text.value: Here is the honest split. Getting good at what you teach took you years. Call it your ten thousand hours. Nobody can do those for you and no book can hand them to you. You have already put them in, or you are putting them in now. The blueprint is everything else. Where the attention goes, what you sell, how it gets sold, and who does the work while you sleep. You bring the reps. The book brings the rest.

text.value: The blueprint is laid out in the order my team and I build, in plain words. Nothing is held back to protect a bigger sale. text.label: Text: A blueprint is not a house, and most people who read it will
text.value: A blueprint is not a house, and most people who read it will still want it built for them. That is fine. Some readers look at that and roll up their sleeves. Others decide their hours are worth more on camera and on calls with buyers. Either way you will know exactly what you are getting and why, and nobody will be able to sell you a mystery again.

text.label: Text: One engine, two roads
text.value: One engine, two roads

text.label: Heading: The book and the done for you build are the same Revenue Eng
text.value: The blueprint shows you the Revenue Engine. The build hands it to you running.

text.label: Text: Same engine.
text.value: Same engine.

text.label: Text: There is not a small version in the book and a real version
text.value: There is not a small version in the book and a real version for clients. There is one. We call it the Revenue Engine, and it is how my own company runs. When a client pays us to build it, my team does the work. When you buy the book, you do the work, or somebody you pay does. The parts are the same, the order is the same, and the tests at the end are the same. The whole thing comes down to one line: Attention + Your Product = Dollars. Here is what each of those three words means on both roads.

text.label: Text: Attention.
text.value: Attention.

text.label: Text: Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube are free stages, and
text.value: Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube are free stages, and a podcast costs next to nothing once it is set up. Most people show up on them with no plan for where the viewer goes next. The book starts by having you draw a map: every place people find you around the outside, your website in the middle, and every arrow pointing one way, toward the website. Your first job in the book is to point every profile you have at that one address. On a done for you build, my team sets up every one of your pages to do the same thing.

text.label: Text: Your Product.
text.value: Your Product.

text.label: Text: Attention with nothing to sell is just a crowd. You already
text.value: Attention with nothing to sell is just a crowd. You already know something people want to learn, and most of you have never put it in a form a stranger can buy. The book has a chapter on exactly that: taking what you know and packaging it into something with a name and a price. On a done for you build we do the packaging with you. That starts with your own e-book, made the way this one was, with your name on the cover, sold on your website. Then your own podcast, produced by our team, living on that same website.

text.label: Text: Dollars.
text.value: Dollars.

text.label: Text: Almost nobody buys the first time they hear from you. It tak
text.value: Almost nobody buys the first time they hear from you. It takes seven to ten times. The Revenue Engine is six business systems that keep you in front of a person until they are ready: Premium Smart Websites, the Automated Organic Content Engine, Speed to Lead, Automated Five Star Reviews, Database Reactivation, and Paid Ads = Booked Appointments, added last. Together they sort, sift and funnel your audience from a follower to a paying client. The book gives each system its own chapter. The build hands you all six, connected and already running.

text.label: Text: AI employees.
text.value: AI employees.

text.label: Text: You used to need a payroll full of people to do this. AI emp
text.value: You used to need a payroll full of people to do this. AI employees do that work now, day and night. They answer the messages, follow up with the people who went quiet, and ask every client for a review without anybody having to remember. The book shows you how to put them to work yourself, including one taught to speak for you in your own words. I call that one your AI twin. On a done for you build, my team sets them up, teaches them how you talk, and reads their conversations so they keep getting better.

text.label: Text: A talent agency.
text.value: A talent agency.

text.label: Text: Talent used to need radio, TV and somebody at the gate to sa
text.value: Talent used to need radio, TV and somebody at the gate to say yes. You couldn't even get into that space. Free social media and a podcast that costs next to nothing flipped that. Anybody can be seen now. What you still need is somebody behind you who knows how to turn being seen into being paid. That is what my company is: a modern day talent agency. We teach you self-promotion, package what you know, and show you how to sell it with a modern website and sales system. That sales system is the Revenue Engine. The book is that same job, written down.

text.label: Text: The only difference.
text.value: The only difference.

text.label: Text: Who does the hours, and what comes with it. With the book, t
text.value: Who does the hours, and what comes with it. With the book, the hours are yours or your helper's. You open the accounts, follow the steps and run the tests. With the build, the hours are ours. My team builds every system, writes and produces your e-book with you, produces your podcast, hands it all over, and then keeps it running every month. You get a US company with a team behind the work, and you get me on your account. You get a copy of my business, front to back, with your name on it.

text.label: Text: What is the same.
text.value: What is the same.

text.label: Text: What you end up owning. The website is yours. The list of pe
text.value: What you end up owning. The website is yours. The list of people who raised their hand is yours. What you know, and the product you made from it, are yours. That is true if you build it from the book on a Saturday. It is true if your assistant builds it from the book. And it is true if my team builds it. The social platforms stay what they always were, free stages you use on purpose. The place the money changes hands belongs to you on every road.

text.label: Text: Why we sell both.
text.value: Why we sell both.

text.label: Text: Because you should understand a thing before you spend real
text.value: Because you should understand a thing before you spend real money on it. I don't see anybody else writing the whole method down and handing it over before the sale. I would sooner put it in your hands for $495.00 and let you decide with your eyes open. If you read it and build it, good. If you read it and apply to have us build it, you come to the first call already knowing what each system does, and we spend that call on your business instead of on explaining ours.

text.label: Text: Written for a stranger.
text.value: Written for a stranger.

text.label: Text: I wrote this for somebody who has never seen a system like t
text.value: I wrote this for somebody who has never seen a system like this, because most people have not. None of it is new. Nobody ever explained it to you. So there are no engineer words, and nothing assumes you know what came before. Every build chapter is laid out the same way, so you always know where you are: what this system does for you, what you need before you start, what you rent and what it costs, the steps, how you know it is working, what to do the first week, and the mistakes that waste money.

text.label: Text: Part One, the why.
text.value: Part One, the why.

text.label: Text: You learn why a following by itself does not pay you, and wh
text.value: You learn why a following by itself does not pay you, and what rented land means. I tell you what happened to my own book when I put it on somebody else's property. Then you get the map. By the end of Part One you can draw your own map on a single sheet of paper, see which arrows are missing, and point every profile you have at one address. That alone is a job many people with a big following have never done, and you can do it before you spend a dollar on anything else.

text.label: Text: Packaging what you know.
text.value: Packaging what you know.

text.label: Text: Before you build anything, you need something to sell. One c
text.value: Before you build anything, you need something to sell. One chapter walks you through taking what is in your head and turning it into a product a stranger can understand and buy. Who it is for. What it does for them. What you call it. If you already sell a program, a course or a book, this chapter sharpens it. If you have an audience and nothing to offer them yet, this is the chapter that ends that. After it you can say what you sell in a sentence, and that sentence goes on your website.

text.label: Text: Own and rent.
text.value: Own and rent.

text.label: Text: One chapter comes before the building, and it saves you the
text.value: One chapter comes before the building, and it saves you the most money. It lists what you own and what you rent, names the job each rented account does, and tells you what the whole thing costs each month before you sign up for any of it. It also gives you one rule I will not bend on. Every account is opened in your name, with your card on it. A helper gets invited in and can be removed. When you finish this chapter you know your real monthly number and you know nobody can walk off with your front door.

text.label: Text: The website.
text.value: The website.

text.label: Text: The first system, and the one every other system plugs into.
text.value: The first system, and the one every other system plugs into. The chapter takes you through the page a follower lands on: your story, what you sell, the proof, and a way to book a call or buy right there. You learn what has to be on it and what does not belong. You finish with a test you run on your own phone, as if you were a stranger who just tapped the link in your profile. After this chapter your followers finally have somewhere to go, and you own the ground they are standing on.

text.label: Text: The content engine.
text.value: The content engine.

text.label: Text: This is how you show up every day without it eating your lif
text.value: This is how you show up every day without it eating your life. You sit down once and record what you teach. That one recording becomes the week's videos, clips and episodes on every platform you are on, and every one of them points back to your website. The chapter gives you the setup you do once and the weekly recipe you repeat. After it, you know exactly what you record, what gets cut from it, where it goes out, and how to tell whether people are coming to your website from it.

text.label: Text: Speed to Lead.
text.value: Speed to Lead.

text.label: Text: When a person comments, sends a message or fills in a form,
text.value: When a person comments, sends a message or fills in a form, they are interested right now. A day later they have moved on. This chapter shows you how to put an AI employee on every door so each person gets an answer in seconds, day or night, in your words, and gets offered a time on your calendar. After it, buyers get an answer while they are still interested, and you stop being the person who has to answer every message yourself for a sale to happen.

text.label: Text: Reviews and old names.
text.value: Reviews and old names.

text.label: Text: Two chapters, two of the easiest wins. The first makes sure
text.value: Two chapters, two of the easiest wins. The first makes sure every client, student and reader gets asked for a review, every time, with nobody remembering, so the next buyer sees proof. The second goes back to the names you already have: everyone who followed, bought once or asked a question and went quiet. It tells you what the first message says and how the replies get worked. That is where the cross-sells and upsells live. Easiest money you'll ever make, because you already earned that attention once.

text.label: Text: Paid ads, last.
text.value: Paid ads, last.

text.label: Text: Ads get their own chapter and it comes at the end on purpose
text.value: Ads get their own chapter and it comes at the end on purpose. An ad sends more people into whatever is behind it. If what is behind it leaks, you pay to lose people faster. So you build the rest first. The chapter shows you how to add advertising once the free attention is turning into buyers, what to watch, and when to turn the ads off. After it, you can tell the difference between an ad that is buying you booked calls and one that is only buying you views.

text.label: Text: Your AI twin.
text.value: Your AI twin.

text.label: Text: Your followers want more of you, and there is one of you. Fo
text.value: Your followers want more of you, and there is one of you. For a long time the only fix was hiring people. Now an AI employee can speak for you. It also shows you how to practise with it before it ever talks to a stranger. After it, a person can ask a question on your website at two in the morning and get an answer that sounds like you.

text.label: Text: paragraph 1
text.value: A store would cap what we can charge for it at $200.00, keep most of that, and keep your name. Read that last part twice. When a store sells a book, the store knows who bought it and the author does not. He never gets the name or the email, so he can never speak to his own reader again. So we sell it on the website we own, and the only thing we rent is the card processor. We know who our readers are, the same way you should know yours.

text.label: Text: paragraph 2
text.value: Musicians and actors have been handing most of their money to the company in the middle for as long as there has been a middle. The label owned the record. The studio owned the film. The talent did the work and got what was left. That is the old kind of talent business. Ours is the modern day kind, and in it the talent owns the website, the list and the product. Social media was never free either: the advertising paid for it, and you were what was sold. Every hour you spend building a following there, you are building on somebody else's property. They can change the rules or shut your account off tomorrow, and your audience goes with it.

text.label: Text: paragraph 3
text.value: This book shows you how to turn that around. Use the free platforms on purpose, and send the attention to the place you own. You still show up on Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube, because that is where people are and it costs you nothing. The difference is that every video, clip and episode now has one job, which is to send a person to your website. That is where they leave a name, where they can buy, and where nobody stands between you and them. Buying this book on our website is that idea at work, with you on the other side of it.

text.value: A talent agent's first job is to look at somebody and see what the public would pay for, often before that person sees it. You are standing too close to what you know to see it clearly. Chapter two has you do that job for yourself. The rest of the book is the other half of the work: the self-promotion, the packaging, and the website and sales system that sells it. I don't see anybody else putting all of that in one place. So I did.

text.value: Read the book if you have an assistant or a team member who is good with a computer. text.value: Have my team build it if you are a coach, an author or an influencer who already sells what you know, and you have a small team in place. You have an audience. You have a program, a course or a book that people already buy. What you do not have is hours. Every message, every sale and every client lands on your phone. Your time is worth more on camera and on calls with buyers than it is opening accounts and connecting systems. That is the person the done for you build exists for.

text.label: Text: What a modern day talent agent does. My team and I build all
text.value: What a modern day talent agent does. My team and I build all six systems on a website you own. We put your AI employees to work, connect everything so it runs as one Revenue Engine, and hand it all over. Then we keep it running. You get a copy of my business, front to back, with your name on it, and me on your account.

text.value: Done for you does not mean you disappear. Two jobs cannot be handed to anybody. text.label: Text: Neither is the reader I wrote it for. Where a technical word
text.value: Neither is the reader I wrote it for. Where a technical word appears, its meaning is attached in the next breath. You never have to read code. But I will not tell you every step is easy. The book says plainly that a few steps are ones most readers hand to a builder, and it tells you what kind of person to hire and what must be true when they finish. Your part is the writing, the deciding and the testing. If you can use your phone and follow a list, you can do your part.

text.label: Text: Then chapter two is your chapter, and it comes before any bu
text.value: Then chapter two is your chapter, and it comes before any building for that reason. You need the sheet from chapter one, a phone that records your voice, and an afternoon. You talk through how you do what you do, turn the recording into a list of steps, pick one box to put it in, name it and price it. The book tells you to sell the first simple version before you polish it. If you have an audience and nothing to offer them, this is where that ends.

text.label: Text: My following is small.
text.value: My following is small.

text.label: Text: The book was written for you as much as for the person with
text.value: The book was written for you as much as for the person with 50,000 followers. You build the middle first, so nobody you ever reach has nowhere to go. Then the content engine builds the attention. I am honest in the book about what that means. It is slower than ads, and you should count in months. I make you no promise about how many people will show up. I will say this. When five messages a month is all you get, you cannot afford to lose one, and the plan is built so each one gets an answer.

text.label: Text: How long to read.
text.value: How long to read.

text.label: Text: It is a book, not an encyclopedia, and Part One is short on
text.value: It is a book, not an encyclopedia, and Part One is short on purpose. I am not going to give you a number of hours, because I do not know how you read. Building is a different question. Every build chapter has its own first-week list. One step waits on the phone carriers and you cannot hurry it, which is why the book has you send that paperwork in early. And attention takes months. I will not give you a date by which it is all running. Be careful of anybody who does.

text.label: Text: What I need to start.
text.value: What I need to start.

text.label: Text: Less than you think. A phone. A laptop for the building. One
text.value: Less than you think. A phone. A laptop for the building. One email address you will still have in ten years. A sheet of paper for chapter one. An afternoon for chapter two. One hour a week that belongs to recording and nothing else. You do not need a studio. The book says it plainly: nobody is buying your lighting. And you do not open every account on day one. Each chapter tells you which ones it needs.

text.label: Text: Why a book is $495.00.
text.value: Why a book is $495.00.

text.label: Text: Because of what is in it and how long you use it. A book tha
text.value: Because of what is in it and how long you use it. A book that teaches one idea is priced like one idea. This is the plan for an entire business, with nothing held back, and it goes on working for as long as you are in business. It is also priced by me, on my own website, which is the lesson of chapter three in practice. I would sooner charge what the plan is worth and tell you everything than charge a little and leave out the parts that matter.

text.label: Text: I would rather have it built.

text.label: Text: Then say so, and nobody here will argue with you. A blueprin
text.value: Then say so, and nobody here will argue with you. A blueprint is not a house. The book is the plan, and having my team build it is the house. Plenty of people read the plan, see that it is the work of a team, and decide their hours belong on camera and on calls. This page ends with the two ways side by side. I would still tell you to read the blueprint first. The person who knows the plan makes a better decision about who builds it.

text.value: I cannot promise you a result and I will not. I do not know what you teach, how good you are at it, or whether you will record every week. I can tell you what the book does. It gives you every system, in order, with a test for each one. And it helps you find out early whether people want what you know, by having you say your price out loud to ten people who could buy before you build anything behind it.
